sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F145][F8].

The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022 to $23.0 billion [D131][F5], then fell 5.2% in FY2024 to $23.5 billion [D201][F7] before recovering 9.8% in FY2025 [D236].
The FY2024 decline reflected lower storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,090 million and lower fuel cost recovery revenues of about $526 million [P34].
The FY2025 rebound came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
FPL remains the core, at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], and it contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth that year [D273][D236].
FPL's revenue increase was driven by higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan cost recovery revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
Operating income grew 9.9% a year against revenue's 7.7% [F146][F145], and in FY2025 operating income rose 10.7% on 9.8% revenue growth [D237][D236].
Operating costs grew 0.2pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 10.0% [D257][D249].
Net income CAGR of 0.4% and diluted EPS CAGR of -0.7% lagged operating income badly [F147][F149], reflecting the below-the-line items rather than the operating business.
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sat above the 30.3% window median but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high [F24][D300][D299].
The FY2023 spike of 41.3% was a 23.5pp jump from FY2022's 17.7% [F22][F21][D177], and FY2024 gave back 9.5pp to 31.8% [D212][F23].
The FY2025 operating margin was roughly flat, up 0.3pp [D247], with depreciation and amortization rising $951 million mainly on higher storm cost amortization and plant in service [P16].
In FY2025 net margin of 26.5% sat 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin [F40][F24], as other expense of $3.75 billion and a -17.7% effective tax rate pulled the bottom line [X64][D226].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025 [F64][F32][D227], in line with the 1.91x of FY2024 [D192].
Operating cash flow was 48.4% of revenue [D225], while investing outflow of $23.9 billion dwarfed it [F72], leaving free cash flow deeply negative.
The swing from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million in 2025 [P19].
Stock-based compensation was only 1.5% of operating cash flow [D228], so it is not a meaningful distortion of conversion.
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D231], with net cash at -357.4% of revenue [D232], as total debt grew 15.7% to $95.0 billion [D253][D230].
That net cash position ranked at the 0th percentile against utilities peers (n=4), whose median was -228.4% of revenue [D314][D315].
The current ratio of 0.60x was the window high but still below 1.0x [F128][D305], with working capital of -$9.2 billion [F120].
Free cash flow was funded by debt issuance of $23.4 billion against $10.3 billion repaid [X90][X98], while dividends of $4.7 billion were paid [X82] and the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D251].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x every year, at 0.60x in FY2025 [F128][R1], a structural feature of a capital-intensive utility funded with short-term debt.
This is a liquidity convention rather than distress, given $2.8 billion of cash [F96] and steady access to debt markets.
Net cash has fallen for seven straight years, from -$34.3 billion in FY2018 to -$92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D231][R2].
The steady debt build funds a growing rate base, but it leaves the balance sheet the most levered in its peer group [D314].
The effective tax rate moved -23.3pp in FY2025 to -17.7% [D226][D191][R4], driven by clean energy tax credits that rose about $585 million [P11].
A negative tax rate flatters net income and is unlikely to persist at this level, so the 26.5% net margin overstates underlying profitability [F40].
Whether the operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median [D300] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the post-FY2023 level is durable.
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -357.4% [D232] in the FY2026 10-K would signal the debt build is slowing.
Whether the effective tax rate returns above the 5.6% of FY2024 [D191] in the FY2026 10-K would show the credit benefit normalizing.
